title: Span.__getitem__ hint lookup must not evaluate attribute getters
answers: span['log_level'] raises ValueError instead of TypeError
subscripting a span with a bad reserved attribute value crashes
span[key] error hint crashes when a span attribute is invalid
hasattr on span property raises during error message
body:
Symptom: a user who writes span["log_level"] on a span whose reserved attribute holds an invalid value (e.g. mlflow.spanLogLevel = 999) gets a ValueError from the property instead of the guiding TypeError.
Root cause: mlflow/entities/span.py:Span.__getitem__ probed names with hasattr(self, item), which runs the property getter, and the getter raises while parsing the stored value.
Fix pattern: decide whether a name is a public attribute by membership in dir(self) (item.isidentifier() and not item.startswith('_') and item in dir(self)), which never calls the getter. Only read span.attributes for the dictionary-key hint.
Constraints: any error-path helper that suggests attribute names must avoid getattr/hasattr on properties that can raise; the diagnostic must not fail with a different exception.
Tests: tests/entities/test_span.py:test_span_subscript_with_malformed_property_raises_type_error.
Applies: Span.__getitem__ in mlflow/entities/span.py; the same probing concern applies to any similar hint code in span classes.
applies: Diagnostic code paths in mlflow/entities/span.py that inspect span names; normal attribute access is unaffected.
says: Accessing trace fields with square brackets crashes with a value error on invalid properties.
Diagnostic hints crash unexpectedly when indexing a trace step containing a malformed log level.
Show the proper bracket indexing guidance even if the trace contains corrupted metadata attributes.
Bracket lookup on a trace fails with an internal parsing crash instead of clean guidance.
The error message suggesting trace attribute names should not crash when inspecting invalid values.
search: When generating diagnostic hints for bracket access in `Span.__getitem__`, public attribute names must be checked via `dir(self)` rather than `hasattr`. Using `hasattr` triggers property getters, which can raise exceptions like `ValueError` when stored values such as `mlflow.spanLogLevel` are malformed. Error-path helpers must avoid calling getters via `getattr` or `hasattr` on properties, reading only `span.attributes` for dictionary-key suggestions to ensure a clean `TypeError` is raised. Applies to diagnostic code in `mlflow/entities/span.py` and is verified by `tests/entities/test_span.py:test_span_subscript_with_malformed_property_raises_type_error`.
